title: Residents protest redesign plans at Währing town hall meeting

tea.why: Residents are angry about a local redesign project at Aumannplatz that includes traffic rerouting.
tea.want: They want changes or cancellation of the traffic diversion plans linked to the redesign.
tea.changed: Nov 6: The Greens club chairwoman Raphaela Veit stated they take residents' wishes seriously and plan to proceed with construction in the spring.

summary: Residents in Vienna's 18th district attended a town hall meeting regarding the controversial redesign of Aumannplatz, which turned into a loud protest. Organised critics and attendees voiced strong opposition to the planned traffic changes and lack of alternative planning options. District leader Silvia Nossek faced booing and calls to take the stage, where critics without microphones criticized the project. According to sources, crowd estimates ranged from over 500 people to around 200 individuals. Following the protests, Green Party club chairwoman Raphaela Veit defended the project, stating that the plans incorporated community input and construction would begin in the spring.

response: According to sources, Green Party club chairwoman Raphaela Veit dismissed the objections, stating that most concerns had already been integrated into the plans and that construction would begin in the spring.

updates.text: Residents gathered at a town hall meeting in the parish hall of St. Gertrud to loudly protest the Aumannplatz redesign.
Green Party club chairwoman Raphaela Veit responded to the protests, announcing that the project will move forward with construction in the spring.
